title: Diraq Establishes First US Quantum Laboratory at Chicago’s IQMP On-Ramp Hub - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Silicon spin-qubit developer Diraq has opened its first U.S. lab in Chicago's IQMP On-Ramp hub, running continuous cross-time-zone R&D with its Sydney HQ as it targets rack-scale, thousand-qubit silicon CMOS quantum systems by 2029.

insights.claim: Diraq, a silicon spin-qubit hardware developer headquartered in Sydney, Australia, has opened its first U.S. research and measurement laboratory in Chicago, Illinois, within the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park (IQMP) On-Ramp program hosted at innovation center mHUB.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Marks Diraq's entry into the U.S. quantum ecosystem and talent pool, giving it closer access to U.S. government and commercial customers relevant to investors tracking silicon spin-qubit competitors.

insights.claim: The IQMP program's permanent 128-acre campus is under construction on Chicago's South Side, with the On-Ramp program providing interim lab access, backed by the Illinois Economic Development Corporation (IEDC).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Indicates Illinois' broader strategic bet on becoming a quantum manufacturing and research hub, positioning the state as a beneficiary of quantum infrastructure investment.

insights.claim: The Chicago facility houses two dedicated cryogenic dilution refrigerators to test and validate silicon spin-qubit chips and cryo-CMOS control electronics, enabling continuous 24-hour experimental cycles by operating across complementary Sydney-Chicago time zones.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A continuous, cross-time-zone R&D cycle could accelerate Diraq's device iteration speed relative to competitors running single-shift labs.

insights.claim: Diraq's architecture uses electron spin qubits in quantum dots fabricated with standard silicon CMOS semiconductor processes, targeting rack-scale systems with thousands of physical qubits by 2029 and ultimately millions of qubits per chip.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The CMOS-compatible approach is Diraq's core differentiator versus superconducting and trapped-ion rivals, framing a cost-effective path to scale worth tracking against actual delivery milestones.

insights.claim: The Chicago expansion is led by Diraq CEO and Founder Andrew Dzurak, IQMP CEO Harley Johnson, and IEDC Chief Quantum Officer Dr. Preeti Chalsani.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Names the key decision-makers to track for future funding, partnership, or milestone announcements tied to the Illinois quantum cluster.
insights.locator: Led by CEO and Founder Andrew Dzurak
